user: And what are the typical timelines?
answer:
What I did: I verified your account, opened the service_not_rendered dispute, and escalated the case to a human reviewer—your case is now open and queued.

What I found (typical timelines from Verta’s process):
- Card-related reason codes: review target is 10 business days.  
- Transfer-related reason codes: review target is 20 business days.  
- Complex cases that involve a foreign acquirer can run to 45 calendar days; you’ll be notified if your case is moved to that track.  
These are target review windows from when the case is opened; actual times can vary by case complexity.

What happens next: the review team will examine the case and we’ll send you notifications at key state changes (and you may withdraw the dispute any time before resolution). If you’d like, I can request an estimated completion date from the review team or escalate this to a human now — tell me which you prefer.

Payment dispute rules
## Escalation on blocked disputes
When a dispute is blocked by a customer-level restriction, the case must be
escalated to a human agent.

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.
